facts.text: Facsimile Cameras was deployed at Chryse Planitia during Viking 1 in 1976.

Two facsimile cameras mounted on the lander captured the first panoramic images of the Martian surface. Each camera scanned vertically while the nodding mirror swept horizontally, building up images line by line. The cameras revealed a rock-strewn, rust-coloured desert beneath a butterscotch sky.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Captured the first colour photographs of the Martian surface, revealing the true butterscotch colour of the sky and the rock-strewn landscape.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Chryse Planitia.
These cameras gave humanity its first ground-level view of another planet; the panoramas remain iconic images in space exploration history.
